Question: Brent has goldfish that quadruple (become four times as many) every month, and Gretel has goldfish that double every month. If Brent has \(4\) goldfish at the same time that Gretel has \(128\) goldfish, then in how many months from that time will they have the same number of goldfish?
Solution:
Method 1: Method 1: Follow the monthly counts

Multiply Brent's count by \(4\) and Gretel's count by \(2\) each month. In each pair below, Brent's count comes first and Gretel's comes second:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Month }0 &: (4,128),\\
\text{Month }1 &: (16,256),\\
\text{Month }2 &: (64,512),\\
\text{Month }3 &: (256,1024),\\
\text{Month }4 &: (1024,2048),\\
\text{Month }5 &: (4096,4096).
\end{aligned}
\]
The counts differ at every earlier month and agree at month \(5\). In the following month Brent has more, and his larger multiplication factor keeps his count larger thereafter. Thus they have the same number after \(\boxed{5}\) months, choice B.

Method 2: Method 2: Compare their population ratio

Initially, Gretel has \(128\div4=32\) times as many goldfish as Brent.

Doubling both populations would leave their ratio unchanged. Brent's quadrupling is a doubling followed by another doubling, so each month Gretel's count divided by Brent's count is halved. Including the starting time, these ratios are
\[
32,\quad16,\quad8,\quad4,\quad2,\quad1.
\]
Both populations remain positive, so they are equal exactly when this ratio is \(1\). It takes five halvings to reach \(1\); further halvings make it smaller than \(1\). Therefore the counts agree after \(\boxed{5}\) months, choice B.
